Q: How to convert a string to lower case in Bash A:

Here is a solution that is portable across most platforms (that I use) as well as older versions of Bash.

I have also been frustrated with arrays, functions and use of prints, echos and temporary files to retrieve trivial variables. This works very well for me so far.

My main testing environments are:

  1. GNU Bash, version 4.1.2(1)-release (x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu)
  2. GNU Bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (sparc-sun-solaris2.10)
lcs="abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
ucs="ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
input="Change Me To All Capitals"
for (( i=0; i<"${#input}"; i++ )) ; do :
    for (( j=0; j<"${#lcs}"; j++ )) ; do :
        if [[ "${input:$i:1}" == "${lcs:$j:1}" ]] ; then
            input="${input/${input:$i:1}/${ucs:$j:1}}"
        fi
    done
done

It is a simple C-style for loop to iterate through the strings.

For the line below, if you have not seen anything like this before, this is where I learned this.

In this case, the line checks if the character ${input:$i:1} (lower case) exists in input and if so, replaces it with the given character ${ucs:$j:1} (upper case) and stores it back into input.

input="${input/${input:$i:1}/${ucs:$j:1}}"

Q: How can I write a regex that can find passwords in texts and binary data? A:

Your mission statement was to find passwords in binary stream. You can parse a binary stream but the data as seen by the regex engine is 1 byte per character. That's 0-255 decimal - the byte. Thats the ascii / extended ascii ranges. Any password characters would only be discernible as a byte. So in binary, ascii strings are packed sequences of 8-bit binary. There is no decoding into Unicode because those characters are > x100. So you are restricted to ascii. Moreover, you can only match printable sequences between x21-x7e to be a realistic non-whitespace password.

Q: reliably stop bash find after n matches A:

Using parallel, this fits my requirement

find . -type f -iname "*.txt" | head -n 10 | parallel -j1 'myscript.sh {}  '

Q: Java 21 + Micronaut 4.10.9 + Ignite 3.0: ClassNotFoundException: io.micronaut.core.convert.DefaultConversionService A:

This is not your persistence/RocksDB config. The root cause is binary incompatibility:

Apache Ignite RestComponent imports/uses:

io.micronaut.core.convert.DefaultConversionService

in its embedded Micronaut REST server code.

But in Micronaut 4.x, the public conversion API is centered on ConversionService.SHARED, not that old DefaultConversionService class. So Ignite’s REST module was built against an older Micronaut API, while your app runs Micronaut 4.10.9.

Also note your log says:

Apache Ignite ver. 3.1.0-SNAPSHOT

not 3.0. That matters: you may be mixing Ignite artifacts/SNAPSHOTs.

Practical fixes

Best option: do not embed Ignite 3 server inside the same Micronaut 4 app. Run Ignite as a separate node/process/container and connect from Micronaut using the Ignite client. Ignite’s own docs expose management through REST on port 10300, configurable under ignite.rest.

If you must embed it:

configurations.all {
    resolutionStrategy.eachDependency {
        if (requested.group == "io.micronaut") {
            useVersion("3.10.4") // or the exact Micronaut version Ignite was built/tested with
        }
    }
}

But that usually conflicts with a Micronaut 4 app, so I would avoid it.

Also check your dependency tree:

./gradlew dependencyInsight --dependency micronaut-core --configuration runtimeClasspath
./gradlew dependencyInsight --dependency ignite --configuration runtimeClasspath

You likely need either:

  1. Micronaut 4 app + external Ignite server + Ignite client, recommended; or

  2. Embedded Ignite + Micronaut version aligned to Ignite’s internal REST dependency, risky; or

  3. Disable/exclude Ignite REST only if Ignite 3 allows your use case without it.

The key line is:

NoClassDefFoundError: io/micronaut/core/convert/DefaultConversionService

So the fix is dependency/version isolation, not storage configuration.

Q: Android Buildozer failed A:

Problems Solved

Use the workflow below. It fully automates the build process accepting the licenses vanishing all errors during the apk build.

# Sample repository at https://github.com/Novfensec/SAMPLE-KIVYMD-APP

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2

      # Used to cache dependencies with a timeout
      - name: Get Date
        id: get-date
        run: |
          echo "::set-output name=date::$(/bin/date -u "+%Y%m%d")"
        shell: bash

      - name: Cache Buildozer global directory
        uses: actions/cache@v2
        with:
          path: .buildozer_global
          key: buildozer-global-${{ hashFiles('buildozer.spec') }}

      - uses: actions/cache@v2
        with:
          path: .buildozer
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.get-date.outputs.date }}-${{ hashFiles('buildozer.spec') }}

      # Install dependencies
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            build-essential \
            git \
            ffmpeg \
            libsdl2-dev \
            libsdl2-image-dev \
            libsdl2-mixer-dev \
            libsdl2-ttf-dev \
            libportmidi-dev \
            libswscale-dev \
            libavformat-dev \
            libavcodec-dev \
            libunwind-dev \
            zlib1g-dev
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libsqlite3-dev \
            sqlite3 \
            bzip2 \
            libbz2-dev \
            zlib1g-dev \
            openssl \
            libgdbm-dev \
            libgdbm-compat-dev \
            liblzma-dev \
            libreadline-dev \
            uuid-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0 \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-good
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            zip \
            unzip \
            autoconf \
            libtool \
            pkg-config \
            libncurses5-dev \
            libncursesw5-dev \
            libtinfo5 \
            cmake \
            libffi-dev \
            libssl-dev \
            automake

      # Set up Java 17 required by Gradle
      - name: Setup Java 17 required by Gradle
        uses: actions/setup-java@v3
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'  # or 'zulu', 'liberica', etc.
          java-version: '17'

      # Set up Python
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v2
        with:
          python-version: '3.8' #set your python version

      # Install pip dependencies
      - name: Install pip dependencies
        run: |
          pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install buildozer cython==0.29.33

      # Build with Buildozer
      - name: Build with Buildozer
        id: buildozer
        run: |
          yes | buildozer -v android debug

      # Upload artifacts
      - name: Upload APK artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: package
          path: bin/*.apk
